prompt.context: The 3rd largest athletic shoe company in the US has hired your consulting firm to determine why its profits are declining while the profits of its two competitors are growing.
prompt.question: Why are the client's profits declining, and what should the company do to reverse the trend?

clarifying_info.q: Are the client's costs in line with those of its competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, costs — including manufacturing, distribution, and G&A — all appear to be in line with competitors. Costs are not the problem.
Yes, revenue is down 6% from last year, and projections show another 5% dip for the coming year.

clarifying_info.q: Are sales of certain shoe models declining disproportionately?
clarifying_info.a: No, most SKUs are declining at a similar rate across the board.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the client's biggest customers / target demographic?
clarifying_info.a: Formerly, the biggest customers were serious athletes interested in high-performance shoes. The company is no longer sure if that is still true.

framework: Profits = Revenues – Costs: first check each side independently
Cost side: compare manufacturing, distribution, selling (direct force vs. independent reps), and G&A costs against competitors
Revenue side: diagnose decline by decomposing into price vs. volume, then by product category (SKUs), then by customer segment / demographic
Customer segmentation: identify who is actually buying athletic shoes today vs. the client's assumed target
Strategic response: design a plan to target the highest-value segment identified by field research

questions.prompt: Are costs driving the profit decline?
questions.guidance: Candidate should systematically check manufacturing costs (incl. offshore production), selling costs (dedicated sales force vs. independent reps), distribution costs, and G&A. The answer here is that costs are in line with competitors, so the candidate should pivot to revenue.

questions.prompt: What is happening to revenues, and why?
questions.guidance: Revenue is down 6% year-over-year with a further 5% decline projected. Candidate should break revenue into price × volume, then look at whether specific SKUs or product lines are underperforming. The answer is that most SKUs are declining at a similar rate, pointing to a broad market/customer issue rather than a product-specific problem.

questions.prompt: Who is actually buying athletic shoes in this market?
questions.guidance: With costs fine and revenue broadly declining across products, the root cause is that the company no longer knows who its customers are. Field research (e.g., observing shoppers at retail locations such as Foot Locker) is a practical, low-cost method to identify buying demographics. Research revealed that 13- to 24-year-olds account for 65% of all athletic shoe purchases, making them the priority segment.

questions.prompt: What plan would you put together to target the 13- to 24-year-old demographic?
questions.guidance: This segment is less focused on high performance and more focused on image and style (e.g., celebrity endorsements, brand cool factor). A strong answer recommends a marketing and advertising campaign that repositions the brand as aspirational and image-driven for young consumers, potentially including celebrity/athlete endorsements and updated product styling.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the possible reasons why a shoe company's revenues could be declining broadly across all product SKUs?

categories.name: Customer / Demand shifts
ideas: Target demographic has shifted buying behavior
Brand perceived as outdated or uncool by younger consumers
Customers switching to competitors with stronger brand image
Overall market contraction in the segment the client serves

categories.name: Distribution / Retail
ideas: Loss of shelf space at key retailers
Reduced presence in channels frequented by the target demographic
Competitors gaining exclusivity deals with major retailers

categories.name: Marketing & Brand
ideas: Messaging not resonating with actual buyers
Lack of celebrity or influencer endorsements

categories.name: Product
ideas: Product design seen as functional but not fashionable
Failure to track evolving style trends
Competitors offering better aesthetics at similar price points

recommendation: The root cause of declining profits is a revenue problem driven by a customer identity gap: the client has been targeting serious athletes, but the dominant buying group (65% of purchases) is 13- to 24-year-olds who prioritize image over performance

The company should pivot its marketing and product positioning to target this demographic, emphasizing brand image, style, and aspirational appeal (e.g., celebrity endorsements, culturally relevant advertising)
risks: Alienating the existing serious-athlete customer base if the brand repositioning is too abrupt
Repositioning may take time, during which revenue continues to decline
Competitors may respond with increased marketing spend targeting the same demographic
next_steps: Conduct deeper quantitative market research to size the 13-24 segment and understand their brand preferences
Develop a brand repositioning strategy and advertising campaign tailored to the youth demographic
Evaluate potential celebrity or athlete endorsement partnerships
Review product design pipeline to ensure new styles align with youth fashion trends
